newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open sharply lower on Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open sharply lower on Wall Street.

text.p: French shares opened sharply lower on Thursday on the back of an overnight fall on Wall Street and ahead of key unemployment data in the United States on Friday.

Shares in Generale des Eaux and Havas were suspended pending a statement. The two companies are scheduled to hold a news conference at 1630 GMT where they are expected to announce a deal concerning their stakes in cable TV company Canal Plus. Canal Plus shares were down 1.45 percent at 1,155 francs.
The bourse's blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 19.89 points or 0.78 percent at 2,521.36 at 0921 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract fell to 2528 from 2546.5 at Wednesday's close.

Shares in chemicals group Rhone-Poulenc were down 3.04 percent after state agency Consortium de Realisation said it had sold a 4.6 percent stake in Rhone. Fund managers said the shares were placed at 177.50 francs each.
Shares in skincare and cosmetics firm Clarins were down 1.29 percent at 765 francs after the company announced a convertible bond issue totalling between 890 million and 1.02 billion francs.
